original_title: Automated cassette-based production, purification, and radiolabeling of [(89)Zr]Zr-DFO-trastuzumab.
title: An automated cassette for making Zr-89-trastuzumab
blurb: One cassette handles production, purification, and radiolabeling of Zr-89-DFO-trastuzumab, the standard immuno-PET tracer for tracking HER2. Not a new tracer, just taking the manual radiochemistry out of the loop so more sites can actually run it.

original_title: Targeting cancer immune evasion with anti-FOLR1 antibody-drug conjugate potentiates anti–PD-1 efficacy in colorectal cancer
title: An anti-FOLR1 ADC that makes anti-PD-1 work harder
blurb: The point isn't that the anti-FOLR1 antibody-drug conjugate kills colorectal cancer cells, it's that doing so also disables the tumor's immune evasion trick, which is what lets the anti-PD-1 checkpoint drug outperform itself alone.

original_title: Piezocatalytic Sulfonation Enables Nongenetic Competition Therapy for Colorectal Cancer
title: Ultrasound-triggered protein sulfonation, no genes involved
blurb: A hyaluronic-acid-coated KNN-gold piezoelectric nanoparticle turns ultrasound into a piezo-potential that drives charge separation and sulfonates a protein in place, an irreversible modification normally hard to impose inside living cells. Applied here as a nongenetic competition therapy against colorectal cancer, sound doing the job an enzyme usually would.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Efficacy and safety of [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE versus standard systemic therapies in advanced well-differentiated gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors: a retrospective cohort study.
title: Lu-177-DOTATATE sized up against standard GEP-NET care
blurb: A retrospective cohort comparing Lu-177-DOTATATE to standard systemic therapies for advanced, well-differentiated gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, on both efficacy and safety. Retrospective, not randomized, so it's real-world signal rather than trial-grade proof.

original_title: Click-Assembled Coumarin-BODIPY Conjugate as a Heavy-Atom-Free Photosensitizer for Chemo-Photodynamic Therapy.
title: A coumarin-BODIPY click conjugate that skips the heavy atoms
blurb: Photosensitizers usually lean on heavy atoms to force triplet-state crossing for photodynamic therapy, which brings its own toxicity baggage. This click-assembled coumarin-BODIPY pair gets there without one, built to run chemo- and photodynamic therapy together.

original_title: Engineering Cyclic Peptide FAP Radioligands for Improved Pharmacokinetics and Clinical PET Imaging.
title: A cyclic peptide spin on FAP-targeted PET tracers
blurb: Fibroblast activation protein radioligands tend to clear fast and look messy on scans, so this locks the scaffold into a cyclic peptide to improve pharmacokinetics for clinical PET imaging. No data to judge yet, just the engineering pitch.

original_title: Single-Time-Point Time-integrated Activity Estimation for Dosimetry in 177Lu-PSMA Therapy: Evaluation of Analytical and Machine Learning Methods.
title: Guessing the 177Lu-PSMA dose from one scan instead of several
blurb: Full dosimetry for 177Lu-PSMA therapy usually means multiple time-point scans to integrate activity over time. This compares analytical methods against machine learning for estimating that integral from a single time point, which is convenient if the accuracy holds up against the multi-scan standard.

original_title: Comparison of three interpretation criteria for [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT in suspected pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma of the adrenal gland or retroperitoneal space.
title: Three ways to read a DOTATATE scan give three different answers
blurb: A head-to-head of three interpretation criteria for Ga-68-DOTATATE PET/CT in suspected pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma of the adrenal gland or retroperitoneum. Worth knowing which criteria a report used before trusting its read.

original_title: Rescue of glutaric aciduria type I by GalNAc-conjugated siRNA against aminoadipate semialdehyde synthase
title: Treating glutaric aciduria by muting the enzyme upstream of the broken one
blurb: Glutaric aciduria type I comes from a dead downstream enzyme, so instead of fixing that one directly, this knocks down aminoadipate semialdehyde synthase with a liver-targeted GalNAc-siRNA to cut off the toxic buildup earlier in the pathway. Framed as a rescue, so likely an animal model rather than a patient.

original_title: Membrane-confined self-assembly enables localized bioorthogonal prodrug activation and selective cancer therapy
title: Keeping the click chemistry pinned to the membrane so the prodrug only fires there
blurb: A bioorthogonal prodrug-activation system built to self-assemble and stay confined at the membrane, so the activating chemistry stays local instead of drifting through the cell. The payoff is selective cancer killing without the prodrug going off everywhere at once.

original_title: A Unified Asymmetric Approach to Tetracyclic Diterpenoids via Ring Reconstruction Strategy
title: One precursor, several diterpenoid skeletons, via taking the rings apart and rebuilding them
blurb: Tetracyclic diterpenoids are a mess of fused and bridged rings that normally need a separate total synthesis apiece. Here a platinum-catalyzed diboration/tandem allylation sets the early stereocenters and builds an oxidized ent-kaurane hub, and a ring reconstruction step diverges out to the different scaffolds from that single hub. Neat if the divergence genuinely spans the family rather than just rebranding one route.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Dosimetric and biological characterization of a three-dimensional cell co-culture model for the evaluation of specific and nonspecific effects induced by targeted radiopharmaceuticals
title: A 3D co-culture dish for separating a radiopharmaceutical's real hit from its collateral damage
blurb: A dosimetry and biology workup of a 3D cell co-culture model meant to tease apart radiation effects on the targeted cells from the nonspecific dose to everything nearby. A tool paper, useful mainly to whoever's modeling bystander effects before moving to animals.

original_title: Aldehyde-Hydrazide Crosslinking for Polysaccharide-Amplified Electrochemical Detection of Nucleic Acids
title: Polysaccharides as the signal amplifier for electrochemical DNA detection
blurb: Polysaccharide chains carry hundreds of sites to hang labels off, and aldehyde-hydrazide crosslinking gives a clean, chemoselective way to load electroactive tags onto them. The payoff is an amplified electrochemical readout for nucleic acid detection built on a cheap, stable backbone instead of anything exotic.

original_title: Antibody-Drug Conjugate Targeting Tumor Scaffolding Shows Promise in Trial - Mirage News
title: An ADC aimed at the scaffolding around tumors instead of the tumor cells
blurb: An antibody-drug conjugate going after tumor scaffolding rather than the cancer cells directly, reported as promising via a news aggregator with no numbers attached. Wait for the actual trial data before getting excited.

original_title: Monolith, porous bead, membrane or fibre? A comparative characterisation of four oligo-dT affinity chromatography matrices for mRNA capture
title: Monolith vs bead vs membrane vs fibre for fishing mRNA out of a reaction
blurb: The first side-by-side of all four oligo-dT chromatography formats for mRNA capture, run on both a short eGFP transcript and the much longer SARS-CoV-2 spike mRNA. They screened the loading salt and mapped flow rate, load concentration, and GuHCl concentration to see which format actually holds up once the mRNA gets long, not just on the easy short constructs.

original_title: Toward a Deeper Understanding of Single-Atom Catalysis
title: Single-atom catalysts are a moving target, literally
blurb: The "single atom" in SACs isn't one fixed site, it's a working-state ensemble whose coordination, charge, spin state, and bound adsorbates shift under actual operating conditions. And as the field moves to bimetallic pairs and SAC-nanoparticle hybrids, you get multiple interconverting site families coexisting at once, so the clean structure drawn on paper is already out of date by the time the catalyst is running.

original_title: Photoinduced On-DNA C–S Coupling Enables Access to α-Sulfenylated Carbonyl Scaffolds
title: A photochemical shortcut to sulfenylated DNA-barcoded building blocks
blurb: Transition-metal-free, one-pot, light-driven C-S coupling run directly on DNA, giving alpha-sulfenylated carbonyl scaffolds that were previously awkward to make this way. The useful part is that it works on the cereblon-binding glutarimides used in IMiD drugs and PROTACs, so it's a real route to getting those into DNA-encoded libraries.

original_title: Self-Oxygenated Radionuclide Delivery System for Synergistic Sensitization of Tumor Chemotherapy and Radionuclide Therapy
title: A nanoparticle that makes its own oxygen so radionuclide therapy actually works
blurb: Dendritic mesoporous silica loaded with the chemo drug 5-FU and catalase, the catalase presumably breaking down tumor peroxide into oxygen on site to relieve the hypoxia that normally blunts radionuclide therapy, while the chemo hits the tumor alongside the radiation. Two mechanisms stacked onto one carrier rather than one trick stretched to cover both jobs.

original_title: Stepwise Cross-Linked BSA/Sodium Alginate/Silk Fibroin Composite Hydrogel with Strontium Loading for the Simultaneous Promotion of Angiogenesis and Osteogenesis in Non-Load-Bearing Bone Repair.
title: A strontium-loaded hydrogel trying to grow bone and blood vessels at once
blurb: A BSA/alginate/silk fibroin hydrogel built by stepwise cross-linking and loaded with strontium, aimed at non-load-bearing bone defects that need new vessels and new bone forming together. Strontium's long history nudging osteoblasts is the rationale here, just delivered through a composite gel instead of a single-material scaffold.

original_title: CaMKII generates actin bundle morphology and mechanics distinct from canonical bivalent cross-linkers.
title: CaMKII bundles actin differently than the usual cross-linkers
blurb: CaMKII, mostly known for synaptic signaling, turns out to bundle actin filaments into a morphology and mechanical profile distinct from the canonical bivalent cross-linkers. A structural side-job for a protein usually discussed purely for its kinase activity.

original_title: Comparative detection rates and potential clinical management implications of (18)F-FDG PET/CT and (68)Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT in differentiated thyroid carcinoma patients with thyroglobulin-elevated negative iodine scintigraphy: a prospective exploratory study.
title: 68Ga-DOTATOC vs FDG PET in thyroid cancer the iodine scan can't see
blurb: A prospective comparison of 18F-FDG PET/CT against 68Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT in differentiated thyroid cancer patients stuck in the classic bind: thyroglobulin rising, iodine scan clean. The two tracers tend to catch different lesion types, so which one actually finds the disease here is what decides whether management changes.

original_title: Total Synthesis of (+)-Sulfadixiamycin B via Site-Selective Twofold Csp2–H Amination
title: First total synthesis of sulfadixiamycin B, by hitting the same C-H bond twice
blurb: Sulfadixiamycin B is one of the indolosesquiterpenoid alkaloids with those unusual N-S-C and C-S-C linkages and genuine antimicrobial activity, and nobody had synthesized it until now. The route runs convergently through a dapsone-derived biaryl sulfone fragment and closes it out with a site-selective twofold Csp2-H amination, reusing the same C-H functionalization step instead of needing two separate ones.

original_title: [Efficacy Heterogeneity of Antibody-drug Conjugate and Advances in Precision Therapy for Non-small Cell Lung Cancer].
title: Why ADCs don't work the same across NSCLC patients
blurb: A review on why antibody-drug conjugate efficacy varies so much patient to patient in non-small cell lung cancer, and what that implies for matching ADCs to patients more precisely instead of treating them as interchangeable. A survey piece, not new trial data.

original_title: AXL-Targeting Antibody-Drug Conjugate Shows Potential for Soft-Tissue Sarcoma Treatment - Bioengineer.org
title: An AXL-targeting ADC gets a look in soft-tissue sarcoma
blurb: Early signal that an AXL-directed antibody-drug conjugate has activity against soft-tissue sarcoma, a cancer type that rarely gets a dedicated targeted option. Light on detail so far, the kind of headline worth revisiting once actual numbers show up.

original_title: Brønsted/Lewis acid-catalyzed divergent cascade cyclization of alkoxyallene for the total synthesis of eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids
title: One alkoxyallene precursor, two different alkaloid skeletons
blurb: Eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids are biogenetically related, but every prior synthesis built their polycyclic cores separately. This one starts both from a shared alkoxyallene precursor and branches via a Prins-type acid-catalyzed cascade cyclization, with the divergence point echoing how biosynthesis presumably splits the two families apart.

original_title: Synthesis of a Selective Orexin 1 Receptor Antagonist: Development of a Manufacturing Process─Part 3
title: Scaling an orexin antagonist intermediate from 124 to 224 kilos
blurb: Part 3 of the manufacturing writeup: campaign 1 made 124.3 kg of the key triazolylpyridine N-oxide via copper-catalyzed Ullmann coupling then a peracetic acid oxidation, campaign 2 nearly doubled that to 223.8 kg. They also worked out a Pd-catalyzed Buchwald-Hartwig route with Me4tBuXPhos as an alternative, but never bothered scaling it up, which tells you which route actually won on cost.

original_title: Cooperative Heterogeneous–Homogeneous Catalysis Enables Aprotic H2O2 Synthesis and Tandem Organic Oxidations
title: Picking the right acid shape to make H2O2 directly, in a dry solvent
blurb: A heterogeneous metal catalyst and a homogeneous Brønsted acid working together to make H2O2 straight from H2 and O2 in acetonitrile instead of water. The acid's sterics turn out to control whether you get H2O2 or just water, and swapping to unhindered acids buys about a 20x selectivity gain. The mechanistic story is their own hypothesis about proton-coupled transition states at the metal-O2 center, so treat it as a lead rather than settled fact.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Micellar-Partitioning-Assisted Selective Electrochemical Oxidation of Alcohols to Aldehydes and Ketones in Aqueous Media
title: Hiding the aldehyde in a micelle before it can over-oxidize
blurb: Electrochemical alcohol oxidation in water usually blows past the aldehyde straight to the carboxylic acid. Here an anionic micelle solubilizes the alcohol, ferries it to the anode, then pulls the aldehyde product back into the micelle core before it can get oxidized further. A biomimetic trick for keeping a green aqueous oxidation selective.

original_title: Electrocarboxylation of Benzylic C–N and C–O Bonds with CO2 via a Radical/Radical Coupling Pathway
title: CO2 as both the trigger and the carbon source in one step
blurb: An electrochemical reaction where the CO2 radical anion does double duty: it strips the benzylic C–N or C–O bond off benzylamines or benzyl ethers by single-electron transfer, then couples with the resulting radical to build the arylacetic acid itself, up to 99% yield and gram-scale, including NSAID-related products. One reagent playing two mechanistic roles in the same pot is the actual trick here.

original_title: Pathway Selection in Phenol Oxidation by a Ni(III)−Hydroxo Complex: Solvent and Substrate Control of Proton‐Coupled Electron Transfer
title: Same nickel catalyst, same phenol, different product depending on solvent
blurb: A Ni(III)-hydroxo complex oxidizing phenol gives a plain mononuclear Ni(II) product in acetonitrile, but switch to THF and it forms a mixed-valent Ni(II)Ni(III) dimer instead. Nothing about the substrate changed, just the solvent flipping which proton-coupled electron transfer pathway wins.

original_title: Co-Catalyzed Diboration of Glycals and Selective Functionalization for the Synthesis of Diverse C-Glycosides
title: Two boron handles on a glycal, pick which one to functionalize
blurb: Cobalt-catalyzed 1,2-diboration of glycals gives bisborylglycosides with two C–B bonds sitting side by side, then either one can be cross-coupled or converted to a radical through single-electron oxidation of the borate complex and captured. A flexible way into a range of C-glycosides from one diboration intermediate.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Mn(I)-Catalyzed Three-Component Synthesis of β-Functionalized Nitriles at Room Temperature
title: Acetonitrile doubling as the nitrile source, no base required
blurb: A Mn(I) pincer catalyst couples acetonitrile with aldehydes and a nucleophile, N, C, or O, in one pot at room temperature to make β-functionalized nitriles, with water as the only byproduct and nothing extra added as base. First time this three-component coupling's been pulled off selectively with a base metal instead of precious metal.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Fe(II)-Catalyzed Regioselective Radical Hydroalkylation of Aryl Terminal Alkynes via Hydrogen Atom Transfer
title: Iron HAT catalysis gives you E or Z alkenes depending on the partner
blurb: Fe(II)/HAT catalysis hydroalkylates aryl terminal alkynes with unactivated alkenes under mild conditions, and the stereochemistry isn't fixed: allyl alcohol derivatives come out E, unactivated alkenes come out Z. The authors pin it on the MHAT/radical-addition/SET mechanism switching behavior with substrate.

original_title: Cu-Catalyzed α-C(O)–C Bond Cleavage of Unstrained Ketones: A Divergent Approach to C–N Coupling
title: Cracking open unstrained ketones to wire up C–N bonds two ways
blurb: Copper/O2 cleaves the normally inert α-C(O)–C bond of ordinary, unstrained ketones, then branches: straight to amidation, or through a second decarboxylative step to amination or sulfonamidation. Skeletal editing applied to a bond that's usually left alone unless it's in a strained ring.

original_title: Brønsted-Acid-Catalyzed Direct Deoxygenation of Benzylic and Tertiary Alcohols with Hydrosilanes Enabled by 1,1,1,3,3,3-Hexafluoro-2-propanol
title: Deoxygenating alcohols without the Barton-McCombie song and dance
blurb: A Brønsted acid in HFIP/dichloromethane swaps benzylic and tertiary alcohols for hydrocarbons using hydrosilanes at room temperature, close to stoichiometric silane, no xanthate ester and no radical chain initiator. Still tolerates free phenols and other acid-sensitive groups, which is the part worth noting given how harsh deoxygenation usually gets.

original_title: Tuning the Emissive Properties of EuII-Cyclen-Based Complexes through Changes in the Electronic Properties of Donor Atoms on Pendent Arms
title: Making EuII glow differently just by swapping an arm's donor atom
blurb: Cyclen chelators with pendent chiral and achiral alcohol arms, dialed for steric bulk and electronics, and the EuII luminescence tracks those changes. Most EuII emitter work has stuck to cryptands and crown ethers, so this is mainly about widening the ligand toolkit for things like OLEDs and circularly polarized luminescence rather than one standout number.

original_title: Clinical Study of 177Lu-CTR-FAPI In the Treatment of Patients With Advanced, Metastatic Solid Tumors
title: Lu-177-CTR-FAPI clears its first human trial
blurb: A completed early phase 1 trial dosing 177Lu-CTR-FAPI, a FAP-targeted radioligand, in patients with advanced metastatic solid tumors including pancreatic cancer. No efficacy numbers here, just confirmation the study ran and finished.

original_title: Enantioconvergent Radical Suzuki–Miyaura C(sp3)–C(sp2) Cross-Coupling of Racemic Alkylboronic Esters Via Photoredox/Ni Catalysis
title: Racemic boronic esters, coupled stereoselectively via radicals instead of transmetalation
blurb: Suzuki-Miyaura couplings normally just retain whatever stereochemistry the boronic ester brought to the table. Here LiOMe activation routes photoredox/Ni dual catalysis through a radical intermediate instead, so racemic beta-Bpin aryl ketones couple with aryl bromides enantioconvergently, scrambling the starting stereocenter on purpose and resetting it in the coupling.

original_title: Synthesis of a Selective Orexin 1 Receptor Antagonist: Development of a Manufacturing Process–Part 1
title: Fixing a kilo-scale reductive amination that kept misbehaving
blurb: Campaign 1 made 104 kg of a tartrate salt en route to an orexin 1 antagonist, but the H2/Pd/C reductive amination step wasn't robust at that scale. Swapping to NaBH4 in MeOH ahead of campaign 2 gave a higher-yielding, more reliable process, the kind of unglamorous fix that actually matters once you're past gram scale.

original_title: Highly Stereoselective Synthesis of ( Z )-α,β-Unsaturated Nitriles Using a Bulky Silyl Group
title: Picking your nitrile's geometry with a bulky silyl group as the steering wheel
blurb: Grignard addition to a TIPS-protected methoxyacrylonitrile, then elimination of the methoxy group, parks the new substituent trans to the silyl group by default. TBAF desilylation then delivers the (Z)-alpha,beta-unsaturated nitrile in high yield, with the bulky silicon doing all the stereochemical steering before it leaves.

original_title: Pd-Catalyzed Transient Directing Group-Assisted Selective C4–H Silylation of Indoles
title: A directing group that shows up, points Pd at C4, then leaves
blurb: An amino acid auxiliary serves as a transient directing group for Pd(II)-catalyzed C4-H silylation of indoles, giving the regioselectivity of a directed reaction without ever installing or removing a permanent one. Clean, atom-economical route to silicon-substituted indoles.

original_title: Photoredox-Catalyzed Decarboxylative Radical Addition–Lactamization Cascade of N -Arylglycines with Cyclopropenes
title: Cyclopropenes plus glycine radicals makes fused gamma-lactams
blurb: Photoredox decarboxylation of N-arylglycines generates radicals that add to cyclopropenes and cyclize, building cyclopropane-fused gamma-lactams in good yield with strong diastereoselectivity. Metal-free and redox-neutral, so it reads as a solid new entry in the decarboxylative cascade playbook rather than a new strategy.

original_title: Expanding the Scope of LMCT Photocatalysis: Alkene Functionalization via Chlorine-Radical-Mediated Relay Processes
title: Iron and copper turn chloride into the radical actually doing the work
blurb: LMCT photocatalysis with FeCl3 or CuCl2 sidesteps the usual photoredox demand for a long-lived excited state or matched redox potentials, generating chlorine radicals straight from chloride via homolysis instead. That radical then relays into alkene functionalization, extending what LMCT catalysis can do beyond its established tricks.

original_title: Iridium-Catalyzed Borrowing Hydrogen Alkylation of Ethylene Glycol: Synthesis of γ-Hydroxy Ketones
title: Getting ethylene glycol to do more than sit there as antifreeze
blurb: An iridium borrowing-hydrogen strategy alkylates ethylene glycol directly into gamma-hydroxy ketones, and the same chemistry carries over to longer 1,n-diols and even PEG. The real point is turning a cheap, hard-to-functionalize two-carbon diol into a handle for harder-to-make products.

original_title: Carbonylative Assembly of Strained Dispirocyclic Architectures from [1.1.1]Propellane
title: Cracking open propellane with carbon monoxide to build dispiro diketones
blurb: Strain-release carbonylation of [1.1.1]propellane converts its ring strain plus CO into methylenecyclobutane dispirocyclic diketones in a single step, handling skeletal reorganization and carbonyl incorporation at once. The pitch is less the one-pot trick and more that the diketones work as platforms for further skeletal editing.

original_title: Synthesis of a Selective Orexin 1 Receptor Antagonist: Development of a Manufacturing Process─Part 2
title: Kilo-scale orexin blocker, take two on the salt
blurb: Scaling up this orexin-1 antagonist intermediate from grams to real campaigns: 75.3 kg via alkylation of a chloropyrazine then hydrogenolysis off the benzyl group, then 251 kg in campaign 2 after swapping the tartrate salt for the d-mandelate salt. Not glamorous chemistry, but getting from kilos to hundreds of kilos without the yield falling apart is the actual achievement here.

original_title: Phosphine-Catalyzed Asymmetric Dearomative [3 + 2] Annulation Reaction of 8-Nitroimidazo[1,2- a ]pyridines with Allenoates
title: Breaking aromaticity on purpose, with a chiral phosphine as referee
blurb: A dipeptide-derived chiral phosphine catalyzes a [3+2] annulation that dearomatizes 8-nitroimidazopyridines with allenoates, building chiral cyclopenta-fused products in up to 94% yield and 99% ee under mild conditions. The dearomatized products apparently feed into further downstream chemistry, which is the more interesting part if it pans out.

original_title: Mineralized hydrogels for bone defect repair: advances, mechanisms, and challenges
title: Where the field stands on getting hydrogels to grow bone mineral
blurb: A review rounding up the three ways people get hydrogels to mineralize for bone repair: pre-loading the mineral, growing it in situ, or coaxing it in with external triggers. In situ comes out ahead on matrix-mineral integration, for whatever that's worth when none of these have left the lab yet.

original_title: 4DPAIPN/Copper Dual-Catalyzed Chlorosulfonylation of gem -Difluoroallenes under Visible Light Irradiation
title: Visible light turns difluoroallenes into CF2-sulfones
blurb: A 4DPAIPN/copper dual catalytic system adds sulfonyl chlorides or bromides across gem-difluoroallenes under visible light, giving CF2X alkenyl sulfones straight from off-the-shelf sulfonyl halides. Mild conditions and broad tolerance on both coupling partners, by the authors' own account.

original_title: Correction: Site-Specific Native Antibody-Conjugated Microbubbles for Molecular Ultrasound Imaging of Hepatocellular Carcinoma
title: Correction notice on the antibody-microbubble ultrasound paper
blurb: A correction to the earlier work on site-specific antibody-conjugated microbubbles for molecular ultrasound imaging of hepatocellular carcinoma.

original_title: Flash Communication: On-Complex Assembly of Organic Azide Ligands
title: Building explosive azides on the metal, so you never have to touch them
blurb: Instead of synthesizing organic azides separately and then binding them to a metal, this builds them in place by alkylating a complex that already carries an inorganic azide ligand, shown on Rh2 complexes. Skips isolating and handling compounds that are, by nature, volatile and happy to detonate.

original_title: Bicytochalasins A–E: TRAIL-Sensitizing Cytochalasan Dimers Incorporating an Open-Chain Monomer from Phoma multirostrata XJ-2-1
title: Fungal metabolite dimers that make tumor cells listen to TRAIL
blurb: Five new cytochalasan dimers, bicytochalasins A-E, pulled from an endophytic fungus, each pairing a standard tricyclic cytochalasan unit with an open-chain monomer, the first time that kind of half-open dimerization has turned up. Both resulting skeletons carry a 5/6/14/6 tetracyclic ring system built via intermolecular Diels-Alder, and all five sensitize cells to TRAIL-induced killing, though that's still a dish-level result.

original_title: Two-carbon annulation of primary amines to azetidines
title: Turning plain primary amines into N-H azetidines, no protecting groups needed
blurb: Photoredox and hydrogen-atom-transfer catalysis pull a C-H off a primary amine and alkylate it with a vinylsulfonium reagent, then an intramolecular SN2 closes the four-membered ring, going straight from unprotected feedstock amines to free N-H azetidines. Azetidines are everywhere in med chem, and skipping the usual protect/deprotect routine to get there is the whole point.

original_title: Brønsted Acid Enrichment Around Zeolite‐Encapsulated Pd Promotes Efficient Tandem Catalysis
title: Lining up acid sites right next to the metal instead of hoping they're nearby
blurb: A metal cation-directed aluminum-siting strategy packs Brønsted acid sites close to Pd nanoparticles encapsulated in Beta zeolite, with acid density tunable just by dialing the Pd precursor loading. The usual failure mode in these bifunctional catalysts is intermediates wandering off to side reactions before reaching the next site; putting the acid next door is the fix being pitched.

original_title: Synthesis of a Selective Orexin 1 Receptor Antagonist: Development of a Manufacturing Process─Part 4
title: Orexin blocker manufacturing, part 4: where the two halves meet
blurb: 97.75 kg of the orexin-1 antagonist C4X3256 made in three stages: install a nitrile on a pyridine N-oxide with TMSCN and benzoyl chloride, hydrolyze it to the acid and crystallize it out as the hemi-DIPEA salt, then couple that acid with the amine piece built in the earlier campaigns. Fourth installment of what's clearly a long process report, but this is the stage where the molecule actually comes together.

original_title: Radiopharmaceutical therapy for metastatic prostate cancer: Insights from mechanistic modeling and in silico trials.
title: Running prostate cancer radiopharm therapy as a virtual trial first
blurb: A mechanistic model of radiopharmaceutical therapy for metastatic prostate cancer, used to run in silico trials before touching a patient. Handy for probing dosing questions cheaply, but it's still a model standing in for biology, not a result from one.

original_title: An ibuprofen-loaded ionic-covalent dual-network hydrogel for enhanced wound healing.
title: A tougher hydrogel for ibuprofen wound dressings
blurb: An ionic-covalent dual-network hydrogel loaded with ibuprofen for wound healing, the two network types presumably there to trade off mechanical toughness against sustained drug release. Standard hydrogel engineering playbook, applied to an old anti-inflammatory.

original_title: The Role of Extracardiac Uptake in [(99)mTc]Tc-DPD Scintigraphy in Patients With ATTRwt.
title: Where ATTRwt amyloid lights up besides the heart on a bone scan
blurb: Looks at extracardiac uptake on Tc-99m-DPD scintigraphy in wild-type ATTR patients, i.e. where the tracer shows up outside the heart it's nominally imaging. Only useful if that extracardiac signal turns out to mean something diagnostically rather than just being scatter.

original_title: Crystal structure of the first de novo designed phosphotriesterase ZAPP-1
title: ZAPP-1's crystal structure matches its AI blueprint almost exactly
blurb: ZAPP-1, the first de novo designed phosphotriesterase, built with RFdiffusion3 around a dinuclear metal center and a carbamylated lysine squeezed into a pocket that also has to grip a small floppy organophosphate. Two new crystal structures, at 1.42 and 2.28 angstrom, come in within 0.69-0.71 angstrom RMSD of the design model, about as clean a validation as computational enzyme design gets.

original_title: Iodine(III)-Enabled Photocatalytic Skeletal Editing of Carbocyclic Amides Via Radical–Polar Crossover
title: Inserting nitrogen into strained carbocycles with iodine(III) and light
blurb: A photocatalytic iodine(III) radical-polar crossover that inserts two nitrogens into bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane amides, converting cheap carbocyclic starting material into 2,3-diazabicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes. Catalytic nitrogen insertion into strained C-C bonds has been the hard part, so getting it to work on BCPs specifically is the actual news.

original_title: CARBONYLATION AS A STRATEGIC TOOL: Pd-CATALYZED ACCESS TO (HETERO)ARYLACETIC ACID DERIVATIVES FROM BENZYL-TYPE HALIDES
title: Pd-catalyzed carbonylation of benzyl halides, failure modes included
blurb: A broad Pd-dppf-catalyzed carbonylation survey turning benzyl-type halides into (hetero)arylacetic acid derivatives, with runs scaled past 100 g. It's refreshingly upfront about where it breaks: ester formation competing with methyl ether formation, incomplete conversion, and outright decomposition depending on the heterocycle. Reads more like a map of the reaction's limits than a universal method.

original_title: Zincrius-8: An Automated Multi-Position Flow Reactor for the On-Demand Generation of Organozinc Reagents and Their Direct Use in Negishi Coupling
title: A flow reactor that brews its own organozinc reagents on demand
blurb: Zincrius-8 runs commercial granular zinc through an automated flow reactor to generate organozinc solutions on the spot and feed them straight into Negishi coupling, no LiCl or other additives required. Primary and secondary alkyl iodides convert in DMA at over 90% yield, which fixes the actual problem with organozincs: almost nobody sells them and the solutions rot in storage.

original_title: Dual Transition-Metal Electrocatalysis for Allylic Fluoroalkylation of Unactivated Alkenes Using Fluoroalkyl Carboxylic Acids
title: Fluoroalkylating alkenes with an Fe/Co tag team instead of pricey reagents
blurb: An electrocatalytic system pairing photoelectrochemical iron-catalyzed decarboxylation with cobalt-mediated dehydrogenation to do allylic fluoroalkylation of unactivated alkenes, starting from fluoroalkyl carboxylic acids rather than the usual expensive, stoichiometric fluoroalkylating reagents. Cheaper, more available starting material is the whole pitch.

original_title: Theranostics Moves Upfront: A New Chapter for Radiopharmaceutical Therapy - CancerNetwork
title: Radiopharma theranostics trying to jump the queue to earlier treatment lines
blurb: A trade piece on the push to use radiopharmaceutical theranostics before last-line salvage therapy, not just after everything else has failed. Mostly framing rather than fresh trial data, but it's the direction the field is openly angling for.

original_title: Lattice Carbon Cycling Directs Pathway Selection in CO2 Methanation over Oligo-Ni Supported on Hexagonal Lanthanum Oxycarbonate
title: CO2 methanation catalysts that borrow carbon from their own lattice
blurb: Isotope labeling on oligo-Ni over hexagonal lanthanum oxycarbonate shows the support's own lattice carbon swaps in and out with gaseous CO2, and that swapped-in carbon feeds forward into the reaction intermediates. It's this lattice carbon cycling, not just surface chemistry, that ends up steering which methanation pathway wins.

original_title: Aqueous Self-Assembled Nanotubes from Salt-Bridged Cyclic Homodimers
title: A monomer that folds itself into a nanotube in water
blurb: A self-complementary monomer salt-bridges into cyclic homodimers, which stack into tubes with a pore locked at 2 nm, no scaffold or covalent stitching, just assembly in water. The biomimetic-channel pitch is the usual framing, but a well-defined 2 nm pore from one simple building block is the actual result.

original_title: Cascade Radical Homopolymerization of Isocyanide‐Containing Monomers via Photoinitiation
title: Isocyanides finally homopolymerize by radical chain growth
blurb: Radical homopolymerization of isocyanides has been a standing dead end, they'll copolymerize with acrylates or play C1 unit for a metal catalyst, but not polymerize with themselves. A monomer designed to chain radical translocation into ring closure instead of fragmentation gets the first clean radical homopolymer out of them.

original_title: Investigational antibody-drug conjugate shows promise in advanced head and neck cancer - News-Medical
title: Another ADC takes a swing at head and neck cancer
blurb: An investigational antibody-drug conjugate posting promising early results in advanced head and neck cancer. Call it a maybe until the actual response and survival numbers show up.

original_title: Recovery and resurrection of chiral homogeneous catalysts for closed-loop recycling
title: Recycling chiral catalysts instead of binning them
blurb: A closed-loop scheme for recovering and reactivating chiral homogeneous catalysts rather than treating them as single-use. That's the whole claim as given, so judge it once the recovery numbers are in.

original_title: A Label-Free Method to Quantify Early Stage Amyloid Aggregation via Intrinsic Phenylalanine Fluorescence
title: Catching amyloid oligomers without a label, using the one aromatic residue they've got
blurb: Flow induced dispersion analysis, run in both peak and front modes, reads intrinsic phenylalanine fluorescence to catch transient aggregation intermediates, even in peptides too short on tryptophan or tyrosine for the usual aromatic probes. Fibrils are well mapped already; it's the short-lived, heterogeneous oligomers blamed for toxicity that nobody can see well, and this is a label-free crack at them.

original_title: Most Antibody-Drug Conjugate Trials Are Concentrated in the US and China - Bioengineer.org
title: ADC trials: mostly a US and China story
blurb: A look at where antibody-drug conjugate trials actually run, and it's concentrated almost entirely in the US and China. Worth knowing if you're wondering whose patients and whose manufacturing the ADC boom is actually built on.

original_title: UEFCCS: A Multimodal Deep Learning Framework with Fine-Tuned 3D Molecular Representations for Collision Cross Section Prediction
title: A CCS predictor built on a fine-tuned transformer
blurb: UEFCCS folds molecular formula encoding and fingerprints together with 3D structures pulled from a transformer fine-tuned on [M+H]+ collision cross section data. The target is extrapolating to molecules that don't resemble anything in the training set, which is exactly where CCS models usually fall apart.

original_title: Synthetic Pathway Modulation of Metal Organization in Multivariate Metal–Organic Frameworks
title: Choosing where the metal atoms sit in a multimetallic MOF, not just how much of each
blurb: Same mCB-Co/Ni composition, two different synthetic routes, two different one-dimensional metal arrangements and two different sets of properties despite near-identical formulas. One-pot synthesis normally gives no say over metal sequencing, so controlling the order instead of just the ratio is the actual advance here.

original_title: Design and Benchmarking of CK2α′-Preferring Inhibitors for Huntington’s Disease: The Limits of Structure-Based Isoform Selectivity
title: Structure-based docking tries and fails to pick CK2α′-selective inhibitors for Huntington's
blurb: CK2α and CK2α′ differ at only two hinge residues, so isoform selectivity looked learnable by docking. Across 210 paired compounds the inter-isoform docking score showed no relationship to measured selectivity (Spearman ρ = −0.22), and even restricted to a single scaffold the scoring reversed the real ChEMBL activity ranking. A pretty blunt result against trusting structure-based scores for this kind of fine selectivity.

original_title: Recent advances in flavanone synthesis: metal and metal-free strategies
title: A review of how people actually make flavanones these days
blurb: Rounds up metal-catalyzed and metal-free routes to flavanones, the flavonoid subclass that shows up across medicinal plants and keeps getting reused as a drug-synthesis scaffold. Mostly a survey of where conventional synthesis still drags, long reaction times and mediocre yields, rather than one new result.

original_title: Biochemical selection on conserved glycans yield a cross-species AAV capsid for efficient panretinal intravitreal delivery
title: An AAV capsid that gets into the retina through the eye, not under it
blurb: Gene therapy for retinal disease usually means subretinal injection, surgery, and only partial coverage, because intravitreal delivery gets stopped by the inner retina and capsids picked in one species rarely work in another. They mapped retinal glycans across seven mammal species and found two conserved markers, heparan sulfate on the inner limiting membrane and terminal GlcNAc on photoreceptor segments, and used those invariants to select a capsid that crosses species and reaches the whole retina from a simple eye injection.

original_title: Visualizing surface restructuring and chemical state transitions in Co(OH)<sub>2</sub> electrocatalysts during the oxygen evolution reaction
title: Watching a cobalt hydroxide catalyst rearrange itself mid-reaction
blurb: Operando microscopy and spectroscopy tracking Co(OH)2 nanoplates as they restructure during alkaline water oxidation, with the electrolyte's own impurities getting singled out as part of the story. Catalyst identity isn't fixed once you turn the voltage on, it's a moving target, and this is them actually watching it move.

original_title: Paired Deep Mutational Scanning of Lck Activity and Inhibitor Sensitivity Enables the Engineering of Pharmacological Control of T Cell Receptor Signaling
title: Making a kinase listen to a drug without breaking its day job
blurb: Deep mutational scanning of nearly every single substitution in Lck, the kinase that runs T cell receptor signaling, to find mutants that stay catalytically normal but become selectively sensitive to a small molecule. The payoff is a generalizable way to bolt pharmacological on/off control onto cell therapies without wrecking native kinase function.

original_title: Directed Attachment of Catalysts into the Extended Environments of Soft Photoelectrodes for Hydrogen Evolution
title: Growing platinum nanoparticles straight onto a plastic solar cell for hydrogen evolution
blurb: Photoelectrochemical deposition of platinum nanoparticles onto a donor-acceptor polymer blend (PTB7-Th/P(NDI2OD-T2)), with electrochemistry, spectroscopy, microscopy, and DFT all pointed at the early-stage growth. Hydrogen evolution efficiency climbs exponentially with Pt loading, so the polymer junction is doing more than just hosting the metal.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: SAM-Dependent Precursor Peptide Engagement by Darobactin Maturase DarE
title: An antibiotic-making enzyme that skips the usual recognition tag
blurb: Most radical SAM enzymes that build RiPP antibiotics grab their peptide substrate through a dedicated RRE module, but DarE, which installs darobactin's weird C-C and C-O-C crosslinks, doesn't have one. This maps how it engages the precursor peptide anyway, filling in a mechanism for the growing pile of RRE-free maturases nobody could explain.

original_title: Safety and Tolerability of ²¹²Pb-DOTAM-GRPR1 in Adult Subjects With Recurrent or Metastatic GRPR-expressing Tumors
title: Pb-212 goes after GRPR-positive breast and cervical tumors
blurb: Phase 1 safety and tolerability run of ²¹²Pb-DOTAM-GRPR1, an alpha-emitter targeting GRPR, in recurrent or metastatic breast and cervical cancer. Active but not recruiting, so it's just whether people tolerate it, no efficacy data yet.

original_title: Selective Reduction of Interchain Disulfides in Native Antibodies is an Underexplored Problem
title: Nobody's bothered to selectively reduce just one antibody disulfide pair
blurb: Native IgG1 has four interchain disulfides, two H-H in the hinge and two H-L, but conjugation chemistry mostly just reduces all of them to land on DAR4 or DAR8. Picking off one pair selectively would give finer control over drug loading and open the door to dual-payload ADCs without engineering new linkers or antibodies. Apparently almost nobody's tried.

original_title: Incorporating Noncanonical Amino Acids for Protein Structure Analysis: Site-Directed Spin Labeling CW and Pulsed EPR Approaches
title: Spin labeling grows up past engineered cysteine
blurb: A review of site-directed spin labeling EPR, the standard move of parking a nitroxide on an engineered cysteine and reading out protein structure and dynamics by CW or pulsed EPR, now extended to noncanonical amino acids as the label site. More placement options, same residue-level read on motion.

original_title: Accessing Alkyl Linkers for Macrocyclic Peptide Synthesis via Nickel-Mediated Doubly DeAminative Macrocyclization
title: An all-carbon linker route for macrocyclic peptides that skips the usual thioether
blurb: mRNA display keeps handing drug discovery thioether-linked macrocycles, but all-carbon linkers would be more soluble and stable if anyone could make them without losing stereochemistry or SPPS compatibility. This nickel-mediated doubly deaminative macrocyclization is pitched as getting there, with more amino acid diversity and linker placement than older routes allowed.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Translating patient-derived xenograft tumor growth inhibition data to clinical dose–response prediction for antibody-drug conjugates: a QSP modeling approach
title: Trying to get mouse PDX data to actually predict human ADC response
blurb: A QSP model that folds patient-derived xenograft tumor growth inhibition into compartmental ADC pharmacokinetics and virtual patient population simulations to predict clinical objective response rates. Model-informed drug development has a mediocre track record on ADC efficacy prediction so far, so this is another attempt to make the mouse data mean something in the clinic.

original_title: Microwave-Assisted Carbonylative Sonogashira Coupling of Phenylalanine and Peptide Derivatives: An Alkynone Platform for Heterocycles and Environment-Sensitive Fluorophores
title: Microwave Sonogashira turns phenylalanine into an alkynone toolkit
blurb: Carbonylative Sonogashira coupling under microwave, run on phenylalanine and peptide derivatives without scrambling stereochemistry, installs alkynones that branch into pyrimidines, pyrazoles, and isoxazoles. The alkynones themselves double as environment-sensitive fluorophores and metal-ion sensors, so one coupling step buys both a heterocycle route and a bioconjugation handle.

original_title: Electrochemistry Goes Mainstream: Applications in Modern Total Synthesis
title: Why total synthesis ignored the cheapest redox reagents around for a century
blurb: A conspectus on synthetic electrochemistry's slow crawl from BASF-scale industrial processes into academic total synthesis, where for decades it was the method you reached for only after everything else failed. The claim now is that it's actually mainstream rather than a last resort.

original_title: Quantitative UAV-based gamma-ray spectrometry using a CeBr<sub>3</sub> detector
title: Turning a drone-mounted gamma detector into a quantitative tool
blurb: UAV-based gamma-ray spectrometry using a CeBr3 detector, aimed at real quantitative readings rather than just relative counts, the kind of thing useful for surveying contaminated ground without walking it.

original_title: Targeted modulation of protein post-translational modifications through induced proximity: advances and practical toolkits.
title: The induced-proximity toolkit, now aimed at PTMs instead of degradation
blurb: A review rounding up ways to use induced proximity, the same logic behind PROTACs, to install or remove post-translational modifications rather than just destroy a protein. Practical toolkits more than new chemistry, but useful if the goal is rewiring a PTM instead of ablating the whole target.

original_title: Optimizing and Multiplexing Cytotoxic Payloads in Antibody-Drug Conjugate Design for mCRPC - Galina Semenova - UroToday
title: Multiplexing cytotoxic payloads onto one ADC for mCRPC
blurb: A talk on stacking more than one cytotoxic payload into a single antibody-drug conjugate design for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The usual argument for going dual-payload applies here: two mechanisms beat betting the tumor won't dodge one.

original_title: Selective Lanthanide-Binding Peptides: Molecular Insights into Binding Affinity and Selectivity
title: Peptide tags that pick one lanthanide out of a crowd
blurb: REE separation is usually a solvent-heavy mess with lousy selectivity, so these are lanthanide-binding peptide tags run through fluorescence binding assays, molecular dynamics, and enhanced sampling, then descriptor analysis and machine learning to figure out what actually makes one lanthanide bind tighter than its neighbor. Useful if the selectivity holds up outside the bench, which these studies rarely get to show.

original_title: Efficacy of [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 With and Without Androgen Receptor Pathway Inhibitors for mAPM-R Prostate Cancer: Secondary Analysis of VISION
title: VISION trial, re-sliced: AR inhibitors plus Lu-177-PSMA-617
blurb: A secondary analysis of the VISION trial, splitting out prostate cancer outcomes for patients who got Lu-177-PSMA-617 alongside an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor versus those who got PSMA-617 alone, to see whether stacking the two actually changes the result.

original_title: Hybrid multi-timepoint/single-timepoint imaging for multi-cycle radiopharmaceutical therapy dosimetry: Performance in [(177)Lu]Lu-DOTATATE PRRT.
title: Fewer scans, same dose number, maybe
blurb: A hybrid dosimetry scheme for Lu-177-DOTATATE PRRT that swaps in quicker single-timepoint imaging on some cycles while keeping full multi-timepoint scans on others, tested for how well it tracks dose across a whole multi-cycle course. Less scanner time per patient if the shortcut holds.

original_title: Closing the loop in PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy for prostate cancer: from eligibility to decision-validated treatment.
title: Mapping the PSMA therapy pipeline start to finish
blurb: A look at the full PSMA radioligand therapy pathway for prostate cancer as one continuous process, from screening patients for eligibility through to a validated treatment decision, rather than separate steps handled by separate teams.

original_title: Pharmacokinetic and dosimetric evaluation of [(177)Lu]Lu-FAPI for stromal-targeted radionuclide therapy in triple-negative breast cancer: a preclinical biodistribution and dosimetry study.
title: Lu-177-FAPI goes after the tumor's scaffolding instead of the tumor cells, in mice
blurb: A preclinical biodistribution and dosimetry study of Lu-177-FAPI in triple-negative breast cancer, aiming the radionuclide at the fibroblast-rich stroma around the tumor rather than the cancer cells themselves. Mouse pharmacokinetics and dose numbers only, well short of a human dose chart.

original_title: Late-Stage Diversification of Peptides into Unsaturated Amides and Thioesters via Phosphine–Cyclopropenone Chemistry on Solid Phase
title: Modifying peptides into unsaturated amides without taking them off the resin
blurb: A phosphine-catalyzed cyclopropenone activation that works directly on solid-phase peptides, converting the N-terminal amine or Lys/Cys side chains into aryl α,β-unsaturated amides and thioesters, cleanly E-selective and up to 97% yield. Products that are normally a pain to make, here they just fall out of standard SPPS.

original_title: Colloquium: Isotopes for medicine and fundamental physics
title: What isotopes owe to Maxwell, Rutherford, and Einstein
blurb: A review tracing how today's isotope enrichment and detection technology grew out of three old problems: Maxwell's thermodynamic thought experiment, Rutherford's radiochemistry headaches, and Einstein's questions about quantum probability, and where that history has landed medicine and fundamental physics now. History and context, not a new result.

original_title: Stepwise Proximity Labeling With a Switchable Organophotocatalyst
title: A photocatalyst you can switch off before it tags everything in the cell
blurb: Ligand-directed proximity labeling skips the genetic tag but usually pays for it in noise, since unbound photocatalyst keeps labeling after you want it to stop and there's never enough time to wash it out cleanly. This version delivers a switchable organophotocatalyst stepwise, aimed directly at killing that background without bringing a genetic handle back into the picture.

original_title: Macrophage Lysosomal Stress Drives MMAE Antibody-Drug Conjugate Neuropathy in Laboratory Models - Bioengineer.org
title: Why MMAE antibody-drug conjugates cause nerve damage: blame the macrophages
blurb: In lab models, MMAE ADC neuropathy traces back to macrophages taking up the conjugate and getting lysosomal stress out of it, not direct damage to neurons. A mechanism rather than a fix, but it points at macrophages as the thing to target if you want these ADCs without the nerve pain.

original_title: Sorting reaction pathways to program alkene skeletons
title: One nickel catalyst, four different alkene shapes
blurb: Alkene synthesis usually needs a new route for every small structural tweak. These nickel catalysts instead sort reactions between radical and organometallic pathways on command, pulling four distinct alkene architectures out of related starting materials instead of four separate methods.
